hook: Nadella has served as Chief Executive Officer of Microsoft since February 2014 and was named Chairman of its board in June 2021. During his tenure Microsoft extended its investment and infrastructure partnership with OpenAI and built the Copilot line of AI assistants across its productivity software.
name: Satya Nadella

reading.body:
Since becoming CEO in 2014, Nadella has positioned Microsoft to capture AI infrastructure demand by securing OpenAI as a dependent customer, making Azure the exclusive cloud platform for its models and embedding AI assistants across Microsoft's productivity software.

Nadella's strategy treats compute infrastructure as the economically durable layer beneath AI capability. By coupling a multibillion-dollar OpenAI investment announced in January 2023 with exclusive rights to serve as its cloud provider, Microsoft converts AI model development into a driver of Azure consumption. This mirrors his earlier pivot to cloud computing: the shift from selling software licenses to selling the buildings and power that run the applications. When Microsoft 365 Copilot launched two months later, it did the same at the application layer, making AI feature availability dependent on Azure's availability.

The data does not specify the capital commitments, Azure's current load, or whether Nadella's bets on AI-as-infrastructure will succeed as a durable moat against competing cloud providers. It shows decisions and timing, not outcomes. It also does not indicate whether the productivity software integration will drive new demand for compute or merely redistribute existing demand across Microsoft's platform.

standing.watch: Both cases naming Microsoft remain open on the site's records. The New York Times case sits in discovery with summary judgment briefing already closed, and the Authors Guild class action is in discovery. Both have been consolidated into MDL 1:25-md-03143, and the Authors Guild matter is before Judge Stein. The records show no outcome, no ruling, and no settlement for either. They also show no planned listing, no new company, and no further dispute involving Nadella himself. On these records, what comes next is the resolution of that consolidated litigation and nothing more specific.
standing.record: The site's records for Nadella add up to one company and two lawsuits. Microsoft is the sole company listed, and his position there is the only corporate affiliation recorded. The lawsuits are The New York Times Co. v. Microsoft Corp. and OpenAI, which is in discovery with summary judgment briefing closed on April 2, 2026, and Authors Guild v. OpenAI, Inc., a class action in discovery. Both were consolidated into MDL 1:25-md-03143 on September 24, 2026, with the Authors Guild case assigned before Judge Stein. The pattern running through the record is narrow: a single executive role, a body of AI partnership and product work described in his profile, and litigation that names Microsoft alongside OpenAI. The records contain no other companies, no other cases, and no financial figures for him.
standing.standing: Satya Nadella is Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Microsoft, the only company the site lists for him, where he is recorded as an executive. He joined Microsoft in 1992, became CEO on February 4, 2014, and was named Chairman of the board on June 16, 2021. The records credit his tenure with extending Microsoft's investment and infrastructure partnership with OpenAI and with building the Copilot line of AI assistants across the company's productivity software. Two dated entries mark that work: the January 23, 2023 announcement of a multiyear, multibillion dollar extension of Microsoft's investment in OpenAI, and the March 16, 2023 introduction of Microsoft 365 Copilot. Microsoft itself is listed as a public company in Redmond, Washington, founded in 1975. Beyond that role and those two announcements, the records say nothing about what else he controls or influences.
